literal: Feeling shame because of improper deeds is true modesty indeed; the other kind of shyness is that of beautiful-foreheaded virtuous women.
translation: To shrink in shame from improper deeds is true modesty; all other kinds of shyness are merely the natural bashfulness of beautiful-foreheaded women.
modern: தீய செயல்களைச் செய்ய அஞ்சி நாணமடைவதே உண்மையான நாணமாகும்; மற்றவை எல்லாம் அழகிய நெற்றியையுடைய பெண்களின் இயற்கை நாணமே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet distinguishes between moral shame and natural bashfulness. The author states that true, essential modesty (நாண்) is the shrinking back from committing improper or evil deeds. Any other form of shyness, such as the natural reserve or bashfulness shown by beautiful women (திருநுதல் நல்லவர்), is of a different, non-moral kind. For a virtuous life, it is the dread of doing wrong that constitutes genuine modesty.
